title: FP3 Miss Drill
subtitle: W3.d x2 · W3.e x1 · W4.h x1 · W6.b x1 · W6.c x2 · 7 Questions · ~35 min
purpose: Targeted re-drill on all 5 FP3 miss areas. Two attempts each at W3.d (same-base rewrite) and W6.c (quadratic formula 4ac arithmetic). One problem each for W3.e (extraneous check), W4.h (find a from vertex plus point), and W6.b (complete the square all the way to x-values).

questions.question_html: Solve for x. Rewrite both sides as powers of the same base: \( 9^{x+2} = 27 \)
questions.hint: Rewrite 9 = 3^2 and 27 = 3^3. Apply the power rule on the left side. Set the exponents equal and solve.
questions.feedback_correct: x = -1/2. Rewrite both sides to base 3, then set exponents equal.

questions.question_html: Solve for x. Both sides must share the same base: \( 4^{2x-1} = 8^x \)
questions.hint: Rewrite 4 = 2^2 and 8 = 2^3. Apply the power rule on BOTH sides. Set exponents equal.
questions.feedback_correct: x = 2. Key: rewrite BOTH sides to base 2 before setting exponents equal.
questions.feedback_wrong: 4 = 2^2 and 8 = 2^3. Left: 2^(4x-2). Right: 2^(3x). Set equal: 4x-2=3x, x=2.

questions.question_html: Solve for x and check for extraneous solutions: \( \sqrt{2x + 3} = x \). Enter the valid solution and the extraneous solution.
questions.hint: Square both sides to get a quadratic. Factor it to find two candidates. Then CHECK both in the ORIGINAL equation. One will fail.
solution_steps: Check x=-1: sqrt(1) = 1, but -1 is not 1.  EXTRANEOUS.
questions.feedback_correct: x=3 valid, x=-1 extraneous. Checking back in the original catches the negative side.
questions.feedback_wrong: Square: x^2-2x-3=0, (x-3)(x+1)=0. Check x=-1 in original: sqrt(1)=1 but right side=-1. Fails. Extraneous.

questions.question_html: An absolute value function has vertex \( (-3, 2) \) and passes through the point \( (-1, -6) \). Find a, h, and k. Write in the form \( a|x - h| + k \).
questions.hint: Start with f(x) = a|x + 3| + 2 using the vertex. Then substitute x=-1, y=-6. Solve for a.
questions.feedback_correct: a=-4, h=-3, k=2. Same substitution process as a parabola — just with absolute value.

questions.question_html: Solve by completing the square. Show all steps and find both values of x: \( x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0 \)
questions.hint: Move the constant. Half of -6 is -3, squared is 9. Add 9 to both sides. Take the square root — remember PLUS and MINUS. Then solve for x.
solution_steps: x - 3 = +-2               [take square root of both sides]
questions.feedback_correct: x=5 and x=1. The final step is taking the square root — do not stop at (x-3)^2=4.
questions.feedback_wrong: (x-3)^2=4. Take sqrt: x-3=+-2. x=5 or x=1. Do not stop at vertex form.

questions.question_html: Use the quadratic formula. Write down 4ac as its own step before computing the discriminant: \( 3x^2 - 7x + 2 = 0 \)
questions.hint: a=3, b=-7, c=2. Compute 4ac = 4 x 3 x 2 first and write it down. Then b^2 - 4ac = 49 - 24 = 25.
questions.feedback_wrong: 4ac = 4(3)(2) = 24, NOT 4(3)=12 or other shortcuts. Discriminant: 49-24=25. (7+-5)/6 gives 2 and 1/3.

questions.question_html: Use the quadratic formula. Write down 4ac as its own step. Note that c is negative: \( 2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0 \)
questions.hint: a=2, b=3, c=-2. 4ac = 4(2)(-2) = -16. When you subtract a negative: b^2 - 4ac = 9 - (-16) = 9 + 16 = 25.
